findings.issue: A return can now take the shipping fee because a sibling cancel is in REQUESTED. If that sibling then goes FAILED, the new check blocks the sibling from shipping until the cancel is retried to DONE or the return is rejected. With a refund that keeps being declined, this is the stuck state already covered by the runbook's manual path, now also reachable through a return (a new runbook query is included). The customer may have been refunded the shipping on the return while the sibling has not yet been cancelled. That is not an over-refund, because every line is either returned or held unshippable, but it lasts until the manual path is run.

summary: Delta reviewed: b4c7f44..57e20e6. Now that a return can complete the order because a sibling cancel is in REQUESTED, I found no over-refund. completesOrder counts shipments that are cancelled or hold a live claim (REQUESTED or DONE; FAILED is excluded), the same rule cancelShare uses. So when a return takes the shipping, every other line is covered by a return or by a cancel that is DONE or REQUESTED. shippingAlreadyRefunded checks both returns and live claims, so the shipping is paid only once. If the REQUESTED claim the return relied on goes FAILED, the ship check (FAILED and shippingAlreadyRefunded) now refuses with 409, whether a sibling claim or a return holds the shipping. dropFailedCancel can only run after that check, so the shipment cannot be dispatched while the customer keeps the shipping. A FAILED shipment can never be the shipping holder itself, so the check is not too broad. Retrying the cancel freezes the claim again as completing: the remainder after the return's item part, with shipping set to 0 because the return already carries it. The sum stays at paid items plus one shipping fee, apart from the existing HALF_UP cents that payment-service caps. fullyRefunded counts only DONE cancels and needs every return to be REFUNDED or REJECTED. commitCancel computes it after the shipment has moved to CANCELLED, so REFUNDED is set only when everything has really settled. This affects only the status field; amounts are unchanged. The delta adds no new endpoint, input or dependency. I carry forward the earlier minors (lock taken before the ownership check in requestReturn, PENDING settle watch, seller free text in the customer timeline, AC-4).
